name: Taupe Brown
lede: Taupe Brown is a dark reddish gray first dated by Ridgway in 1912, the darker of the library's two taupe variants and one of the more common colors in our archive.

sections.title: The darker of two taupe colors
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 standard places this hue on plate XLIV, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classes it as a dark grayish purple, block 229 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[dark-umber]], [[reddish-black]], [[warm-blackish-brown]] and [[log-cabin]], at 3.5, 4, 5, 4, 4.1 and 4.7 ΔE [1].

[[denim]], [[navy]] and [[terracotta]] all turn up more often than chance in paintings that also carry this color, alongside [[slate]] and [[charcoal]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to Taupe Brown in 1,117 of 23,781 paintings, about 4.7 percent, as photographed [2]. It plays a shadow in 68 percent of its appearances, the dark note in a composition rather than a highlight [2]. Jerichau, José Gutiérrez de la Vega and several Danish painters of the 1800s all use it well above the archive's average rate, with Jan Asselijn's *Nocturnal Crayfishing* (1610) its strongest single match [2].

The earliest dated match is Juran's *Buddhist Retreat by Stream and Mountains*, from the year 960, nine and a half centuries before Ridgway's plate, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that the name existed that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
